name: blueprint/credential-onboarding
description: The first-run flow for the user's own Cloudflare facts: rh_credential_describe is the auth gate, rh_credential_set stores what is missing (never echoing it), rh_settings_get/set pins the account facts, and one store receipt records the onboarded state. Every Cloudflare scenario starts here.
use_cases: first run before any files/deploy tool
ingredients: rh_store receipt: onboarding:<ts> { refs: { ref: configured }, at }
recipe: gate: describe each ref the task needs (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) -> stop and tell the user which are missing (configured:false is actionable) -> set the missing ones through the supervised flow - the agent never sees the value, only { stored: true } -> pin the account facts: rh_settings_set { accountId, defaultZone, defaultR2Bucket } -> receipt: store the onboarded state with a timestamp
result_kind: configured credentials + settings + one onboarding receipt

invoke_contract.set: { ref, value } -> { stored: true } (value never comes back)

config_variants.refs: per task (files needs R2 keys, deploy needs the API token)
config_variants.settings: schema keys only - the wall applies (below)

pitfalls: describe is the gate and the value never appears in any output - assert that in tests
set returns { stored: true } only - the secret flows one way
the settings schema wall: unregistered keys are accepted by set but never returned by get (live-verified) - only schema keys belong in settings
references are POSIX env-var style uppercase names
a rotated token is an unset + set, and the receipt makes the rotation a fact
local_limits: credentials live in the harness credential provider, not the repo - never commit them
cloud_limits: the user's own Cloudflare account; the onboarding gate is what keeps deploy scenarios safe to even start
